CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for evaluation of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a slight improvement in his sleep quality since the last visit. He notes an increase in sleep duration to approximately 7 hours per night, although he still experiences difficulty with sleep initiation and frequent awakenings, which he describes as frustrating. He continues to take sertraline 200 mg daily and trazodone 50 mg nightly, but he expresses a desire to explore further options to enhance his sleep.
Mr. Smith reports that his fatigue persists, particularly during the workweek, attributing it to both the ongoing stress from his job and the effects of his sleep disturbances. He mentions that his headache frequency remains stable at four times weekly, with intensity fluctuating between 4 and 6 on a scale of 10. He has continued taking amitriptyline at 30 mg nightly, but he feels that the medication has not significantly alleviated his headache symptoms. He reports using ibuprofen as needed, with limited relief.
He has maintained his acupuncture sessions twice weekly, which he finds beneficial, and continues his yoga practice. Mr. Smith has also been implementing relaxation techniques and mindfulness strategies, which he reports have been moderately effective in managing his anxiety levels. However, he still experiences significant work-related stress, which he identifies as a primary contributor to his ongoing symptoms.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 6. Amitriptyline 30 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that project deadlines remain a source of stress. He remains committed to physical activity, regularly attending yoga classes and incorporating meditation practices into his routine. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he occasionally consumes processed foods during particularly stressful weeks.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Persistent difficulty initiating sleep; anxiety manageable with therapy and medication; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Stable headache frequency and intensity; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Notable fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce the tapering of lorazepam use as needed. Schedule follow-up therapy sessions to continue enhancing coping strategies. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg; consider increasing dosage to 75 mg if sleep quality does not improve. Continue melatonin at 10 mg; maintain CBT-I strategies and closely monitor sleep patterns. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: The current regimen of amitriptyline has not provided sufficient relief; consider increasing the dosage to 40 mg nightly. If headaches persist, discuss the initiation of preventive therapy with topiramate at the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue to emphasize the importance of physical activity and mindfulness practices. Consider a referral to a nutritionist for dietary optimization. Explore advanced sleep hygiene techniques to further improve sleep quality.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-03-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment effectiveness, and discuss further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
